events.title: Thank you for Next Fest, and duels worth watching

events.title: Officers who make a name: deeds, titles and court honors
events.summary: Officers now remember what they did in your service, earn titles for it, and want things from you in return. Out today in the free demo and the full game. Guan Yu used to start a campaign as "Retainer, Untested Blade", and whatever happened after that, the History tab only listed experience awards: "Field battle won, +30 XP", once per battle. events.title: A campaign for two: play Three Kingdoms Reimagined with a friend
events.summary: Two players share one campaign as allies or rivals. It is in the free demo now, ahead of Steam Next Fest, October 19 to 26. Since the demo went up, the request I have heard most often is to play it with someone else. I have spent the last few weeks on exactly that. Two people can now share a whole campaign: the same map, the same year 196, and the same rival houses, with each of you leading your own warlord from your own seat. events.title: Closer to the fight: rebuilt battles, single combat and a character of your own
events.summary: The last devlog was about the campaign crises that lead to the great battles. Since then I have spent nearly all of my time on the battles themselves. I played through them as a new player would see them and kept running into things that still looked like placeholders: soldiers that could have walked out of a medieval European game, duels you could barely see, and sieges where nobody climbed a ladder. events.title: Turning Points: make your own Three Kingdoms epic
events.summary: Guandu and Red Cliffs are the kinds of battles I keep coming back to when thinking about Three Kingdoms Reimagined. I want that feeling of a campaign reaching a confrontation where the armies on the field carry the weight of everything that came before them. Who did you bring into your service, and who did you trust to speak for you? How much of your treasury were you willing to put behind an uncertain promise? events.title: Demo update: council plans, contact reports and battle aftermath
events.summary: Council advice now stays with you after the meeting. Before a battle, a new report shows who's at contact. After a victory, you choose what the army does with the losses and spoils. A council plan you can follow When you accept a civil proposal, the map shows the current course and the next order needed to begin it. events.title: A clearer start: tutorials, council and the first 50 days
events.summary: Players told us the opening put too many mechanics and too much text on screen at once. We've reworked the tutorial around the action you need next, shortened the early explanations, and made council decisions easier to understand. The updated 50-day demo is available now on Steam. events.title: Development Update — Taking Command
events.summary: Since the last update, I've been working on a problem that becomes more obvious the longer I play: having plenty of choices is only useful if I can understand them in the middle of a campaign. That has meant bringing officer information together, making the menus feel like part of the same game, and going back over sieges from both sides of the wall. events.title: Development Update — Making the next order clear
events.summary: I kept running into the same problem while testing: the answer was in one place, and the action was in another. I could see that an army was selected without being able to tell which officers were in it. A commission named a settlement in the journal while the map asked me to interpret a different marker. events.title: Development Update — The War Remembers
events.summary: The Three Kingdoms sandbox I want to make As a solo developer, the vision I keep coming back to is a Three Kingdoms sandbox—or maybe a toybox is the better word—that players can truly make their own. I love this period because I have come to know these characters, their ambitions, their friendships, and their grudges.
